summary: The base workplace plus the Flutter/Dart toolchain: a Flutter SDK that is already here, a JDK for Gradle, and fvm for projects that pin a different version.

tools.name: flutter
tools.note: in /opt/flutter and on your PATH, warmed up for web builds. This is the baseline — you do not download it. The version is the one the image was built with; an installation may have rebuilt it with another, so `flutter --version` is the authority, not this line.

tools.name: fvm
tools.note: only for a project that pins another version: `fvm use <version>` puts it in ~/fvm and it stays there

tools.name: openjdk
tools.note: JAVA_HOME=/opt/java; a Flutter build for Android is a Gradle build, and gradlew fetches its own Gradle

tools.name: chromium
tools.note: used by the browser plugin, headless; also what `flutter run -d chrome` needs

sdk_dirs.fvm: ~/fvm — only versions you asked for yourself. The baseline SDK is NOT here, it is in the image.

notes: Flutter is already here and it is on your PATH. Check `flutter --version` before you fetch anything — an SDK in your home is a second copy of something the workplace provides, and your home is written back after every run.
No Android SDK. A build that has to produce an APK needs one, and asking for it is the way to get it — do not unpack platform-tools into your home.
You are not root and apt is not available to you. If a tool is missing, say so instead of building a way around it — that is a request, not a defeat.
